# Incident Report: Koi Stealer Infection — 2024-09-04

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames, 2024-09-04 17:32:31–18:32:07 UTC, ~60 min)
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` / `.jpg` (Suricata/Snort ET alert export, 97 lines / 12 alert rows, cross-verified — identical content)

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.17.0.99 | DHCP, ARP, HTTP, alerts |
| MAC | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 (Intel NIC) | ARP, DHCP |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT | DHCP option 12, LLMNR, mDNS, NBNS |
| Windows domain | bepositive.com (AD domain; workgroup/NetBIOS name BEPOSITIVE) | DNS SRV/LDAP queries, NBNS |
| Logged-in user | afletcher | Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString (172.17.0.99 → 172.17.0.17, port 88) |

Domain controller on the LAN: 172.17.0.17 / MAC 00:23:ae:50:ba:fd, hostname WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com (DHCP server, LDAP/Kerberos target).

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer). Attribution is **signature-confirmed**: the commercial Suricata ruleset fired `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits) plus the companion `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1` (50 hits), both keyed on 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80.

This is corroborated behaviorally: the host performs a bot-registration handshake (`GET /index.php?id=&subid=<token>`) that returns a pipe-delimited bot ID string, followed by a POST containing encrypted binary data (`application/octet-stream`, no readable plaintext), then repeats a `POST /foots.php` checkin roughly every 60–90 seconds for the remainder of the capture (96 checkins total) — a classic stealer/loader panel beacon pattern, using a spoofed legacy browser User-Agent (`MSIE 7.0`) to blend in.

Prior to the stealer activity, GPL/ET alerts also fired on SMBv1/NetBIOS session-setup, IPC$ share access, and a Kerberos principal-name-overflow signature between 172.17.0.99 and the DC (172.17.0.17). These are heuristic legacy rules that commonly false-positive on ordinary Windows domain SMB/Kerberos traffic; nothing in the raw packets confirms actual exploitation (no shellcode, no abnormal payload sizes), so this is noted as **unconfirmed/likely benign domain chatter**, not attributed to Koi Stealer.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**C2 endpoint**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP, no DNS resolution seen for it — hardcoded IP, contacted from victim source port 49813/49816 etc.)

**C2 URLs / gate**
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (bot registration GET)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (registration POST, 105-byte encrypted body)
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (recurring stealer checkin POST, 96 occurrences, ~17:35–18:31 UTC)

**Bot identifiers (from plaintext gate response)**
- Bot ID: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn`
- Sub ID: `qIOuKk7U`

**Malicious User-Agent (spoofed)**
- `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)` — used only on requests to 79.124.78.197, inconsistent with the host's genuine Windows/Microsoft-service traffic elsewhere in the capture.

**Transferred files / hashes**
- None recoverable. All POST bodies to the C2 are `application/octet-stream` with encrypted/non-parseable content; no dropped executable, script, or document was transferred in-band during this capture window, so no filename or SHA256 can be grounded in the evidence. (The initial infection vector predates this capture — the pcap begins with the stealer already running.)

**Anomalous but unconfirmed traffic (note only, not stated as an IOC)**
- TLS SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` observed once from the victim, out of place among an otherwise all-Microsoft TLS SNI set. Insufficient corroborating detail (no alert fired on it, single connection) to call it malicious; flagged for follow-up only.

## Summary
172.17.0.99 (DESKTOP-RNVO9AT, user afletcher, domain bepositive.com) is actively beaconing to a Koi Stealer C2 panel at 79.124.78.197 over plain HTTP on port 80, checking in roughly every 60–90 seconds via `/foots.php` for the full remaining hour of the capture. Recommend isolating the host, resetting afletcher's domain credentials, and blocking 79.124.78.197 at the perimeter.
